narr: Broad east to southeast flow advected in monsoon moisture, which fueled thunderstorms over southeast California. Several storms produced flash flooding.
ev: Water, dirt, and rocks covered Highway 136 southeast of Keeler. A few cars were stranded, and the highway was closed from Lone Pine to Highway 190.
The Nipton Rd offramp from I-15 was flooded.
Highway 190 was flooded and closed 4.5 miles E of Highway 136.
Every road in Death Valley National Park was closed, and several were damaged by flooding as well. One vehicle was stuck in mud near Stovepipe Wells, and the Cow Creek water system was broken.
Highway 62 was closed near Rotary Way due to dirt, debris, and road damage.
A mud, dirt, and rock slide closed Highway 136 at Keeler.
Highway 168 was flooded near Deep Springs College.
The intersection of Lilac and Acoma was flooded. The spotter measured 0.66 of rain in 25 minutes.
Highway 62 was flooded with water and debris between Sunfair Rd and Rotary Way.
Hwy 190 was completely impassable east of Panamint Valley Rd due to a large flow of water, debris, and rocks.
